content: The World Health Organization (WHO) published updated treatment guidelines for drug-resistant tuberculosis (TB) in 2016. These guidelines focus on multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB), providing evidence-based recommendations for drug therapy and management. The publication includes detailed methodologies, policy recommendations, and supporting evidence. The WHO emphasizes that the designations and material presented in the publication do not imply any opinion on the legal status of countries, territories, or boundaries. Additionally, the mention of specific companies or products does not constitute endorsement or preference over others. Proprietary product names are distinguished by initial capital letters. The WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information in the publication. However, the material is distributed without any warranty, and the responsibility for its interpretation and use lies with the reader. The WHO is not liable for any damages arising from the use of the material. The guidelines were developed through a collaborative process involving a multidisciplinary Guideline Development Group (GDG) convened by the WHO Global TB Programme. The GDG met in Geneva, Switzerland, from November 9 to 11, 2015, to discuss and finalize the recommendations. The group included experts in TB and drug-resistant TB, chaired by Holger Schünemann and co-chaired by Charles L. Daley. Other contributors included Farhana Amanullah, José A. Caminero, Tsira Chakhaia, Daniela Cirillo, Kelly Dooley, Luis Gustavo do Valle Bastos, Michel Gasana, Agnes Gebhard, Armen Hayrapetyan, Antonia Kwiecien, Sundari Mase, Lindsay McKenna, Nguyen Viet Nhung, Maria Rodriguez, James Seddon, Tom Shinnick, Alena Skrahina, and Carlos Torres-Duque. The External Review Group (ERG) also provided comments on the draft document before its finalization. The ERG members included Chen-Yuan Chiang, Dalene von Delft, Vaira Leimane, Guy Marks, Norbert Ndjeka, Lee Reichman, and Rohit Sarin, among others. The guidelines were finalized after an iterative process of comments and reviews in early 2016, followed by submission to the WHO Guideline Review Committee (GRC) in March 2016. The funding for the guideline update was provided by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) through a consolidated grant. The WHO acknowledges the contributions of the GDG, ERG, and other WHO staff involved in the production of the guidelines. The GDG members completed WHO Declaration of Interest forms to ensure transparency and compliance with WHO’s conflict of interest policy. Some members declared interests that were reviewed and judged not to conflict with the objectives of the meeting. For example, Farhana Amanullah declared funding for consultancies and grants from the Global Fund and TB-REACH. Daniela Cirillo declared funding from FIND and Otsuka for drug susceptibility testing evaluations. Charles L. Daley declared funding from Otsuka for serving as chair of the data monitoring committee for delamanid trials. Kelly Dooley declared funding for providing expert advice on trial design for TB/HIV and her involvement in various clinical trials. Certain members were recused from specific discussions due to potential conflicts of interest. For instance, Lindsay McKenna was recused from discussions on MDR-TB regimen composition due to her non-commercial support from organizations like the Stop TB Partnership and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. José A. Caminero was recused from discussions on shorter MDR-TB regimens due to his role with the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease. The guidelines also include contributions from regional WHO staff and external reviewers. The document underwent multiple rounds of review and clearance to ensure its accuracy and relevance. The recommendations aim to improve the treatment and care of patients with drug-resistant TB, addressing priority questions identified by the GDG and WHO Guideline Steering Committee.
